lesson.arabic-technical-terminology.title_en: Technical terms: الْمُصَادَقَة, التَّفْوِيض, مَسْرَدُ الْمُصْطَلَحَاتِ
lesson.arabic-technical-terminology.family_en: Terms that carry the concept, and keeping them consistent across a project

table.en: authorisation: what you're allowed to do

steps: A technical term has to carry the concept, not just sound like the English: الْمُصَادَقَة is checking who you are, and التَّفْوِيض is what you're then allowed to do.
Different providers choose different Arabic terms: التَّفْوِيض in one manual can be التَّخْوِيل in another. Note the source, and the term your project uses.
Keep a مَسْرَدُ الْمُصْطَلَحَاتِ, a glossary, for your project, and use each term the same way throughout.

examples.en: This manual uses a different term.

examples.ar: أَضَفْتُ الْمُصْطَلَحَ إِلَى الْمَسْرَدِ مَعَ تَعْرِيفِهِ.
examples.en: I added the term to the glossary with its definition.

why.q_en: Why are الْمُصَادَقَة and التَّفْوِيض two terms, when both are about getting in?
why.a_en: They're two steps: الْمُصَادَقَة checks who you are, and التَّفْوِيض decides what you may do once that's checked. A valid login doesn't open everything, so a translation must keep them apart.

selftest.why_en: Deciding what you may do is a separate step.
دَخِيل is one who has come in from outside.

selftest.q_en: Two manuals use التَّفْوِيض and التَّخْوِيل for the same idea. What do you do?
choices: note both, and use your project's term throughout
pick one at random each time
selftest.answer: note both, and use your project's term throughout
selftest.why_en: Consistency helps the reader; the note keeps the variant.

leads_to.en: Explaining a security idea plainly, with the right terms.

lesson.arabic-technical-docs.title_en: Reading instructions: إِذَا, يَجِبُ, اِخْتِيَارِيّ, تَحْذِير
lesson.arabic-technical-docs.family_en: Conditions, requirements and warnings in technical writing
steps: Read the whole section before you do anything: find any مُتَطَلَّبٌ مُسْبَقٌ, prerequisite, the conditions, the steps and the expected result.
A condition with إِذَا, if, comes with its step: read them together.
يَجِبُ, must, is required; يُمْكِنُ, can, is possible; اِخْتِيَارِيّ, optional, is up to you; and a تَحْذِير, warning, may say a step is unsafe.
Check الْإِصْدَار, the version: a help page can describe something that has since changed.

examples.ar: إِذَا انْتَهَتْ صَلَاحِيَّةُ كَلِمَةِ الْمُرُورِ، يَجِبُ تَغْيِيرُهَا.
examples.en: If the password expires, it must be changed.

examples.ar: يَعْمَلُ الْبَرْنَامَجُ فِي الْإِصْدَارِ الْجَدِيدِ فَقَطْ.
examples.en: The program works in the new version only.

why.q_en: What's the difference between يَجِبُ and يُمْكِنُ in an instruction?
why.a_en: يَجِبُ makes a step required: you must. يُمْكِنُ makes it possible: you can, if you choose. Mixing them up changes what the reader has to do.

selftest.q_en: What does يَجِبُ mean in an instruction?

lesson.arabic-security-explainer.title_en: Explaining security plainly: كَلِمَةُ الْمُرُورِ, الصَّلَاحِيَّات
lesson.arabic-security-explainer.family_en: Saying what a security idea is, with an example and its limits
steps: Say what the idea is, give a familiar example, and say where it stops: no single measure makes an account safe on its own.
Keep identity and access apart: كَلِمَةُ الْمُرُورِ, the password, helps show it's you; الصَّلَاحِيَّات, the permissions, decide what you can do.
Use the right term, and explain it in plain words for your reader.
Check the technical facts with a reliable source, and the language with a reviewer.

examples.ar: كَلِمَةُ الْمُرُورِ تُسَاعِدُ عَلَى إِثْبَاتِ أَنَّكَ صَاحِبُ الْحِسَابِ.
examples.en: The password helps prove that you're the account's owner.
Permissions decide what you can do.

examples.ar: لَا تُشَارِكْ كَلِمَةَ الْمُرُورِ مَعَ أَحَدٍ.
examples.en: Don't share your password with anyone.

why.q_en: Why isn't a strong password enough on its own?
why.a_en: It helps prove who you are, but it can still be stolen or guessed, and it says nothing about what you may do. Security comes from several measures together, explained honestly.

selftest.why_en: Showing who you are is the password's job.

selftest.q_en: Does one measure make an account safe on its own?
selftest.why_en: Security comes from several measures together.

lesson.arabic-incident-summary.title_en: An incident summary: رُصِدَ, يُرَجَّحُ, لَمْ يَثْبُتْ
lesson.arabic-incident-summary.family_en: Keeping facts, hypotheses, actions and open questions apart
steps: Keep apart what was رُصِدَ, observed, what's only a فَرَضِيَّة, a hypothesis, what was done, and what's still open.
Give exact times, in order: a تَسَلْسُلٌ زَمَنِيٌّ, a timeline.
Mark how sure each claim is: يُرَجَّحُ, it's thought likely; لَمْ يَثْبُتْ, it hasn't been proven. Don't name a culprit or a motive the evidence doesn't show.
For practice, use fictional material, وَهْمِيّ, labelled as such, with no real names or secrets.

examples.ar: رُصِدَتْ خَمْسُ مُحَاوَلَاتِ دُخُولٍ فَاشِلَةٍ لَيْلًا.
examples.en: Five failed login attempts were observed at night.
The fault is thought likely to be in the server.

why.q_en: Why رُصِدَتْ, a passive verb, in an incident summary?
why.a_en: It reports what was seen without saying who saw it, and without naming who did it: رُصِدَتْ مُحَاوَلَاتٌ, attempts were observed. That keeps the summary to the facts.

selftest.why_en: The passive of رَجَّحَ, to judge more likely.

leads_to.en: Presenting a small technical task, with its limits.

lesson.arabic-technical-demo.title_en: A technical demonstration: عَرْضٌ تَوْضِيحِيٌّ, الْمُدْخَلَات, الْمُخْرَجَات
lesson.arabic-technical-demo.family_en: Showing a small task, its input and output, and what the result doesn't prove
steps: Pick a small, harmless example on your own computer, with بَيَانَاتٌ وَهْمِيَّةٌ, fictional data.
Say what the task is for, show الْمُدْخَلَات, the input, and الْمُخْرَجَات, the output, and say what you observe.
State حُدُودُ النَّتِيجَةِ, the result's limits: a count of failed logins doesn't prove an attack.
Prepare a مَسْرَد, a glossary, and short notes, then answer a new question without reading a script.

examples.ar: يَعُدُّ الْبَرْنَامَجُ الْمُحَاوَلَاتِ الْفَاشِلَةَ فِي مِلَفٍّ وَهْمِيٍّ.
examples.en: The program counts the failed attempts in a fictional file.

examples.ar: الْعَدَدُ وَحْدَهُ لَا يُثْبِتُ وُقُوعَ هُجُومٍ.
examples.en: The count alone doesn't prove an attack happened.
I prepared a glossary of the terms.

why.q_en: Why الْمُدْخَلَات and الْمُخْرَجَات, plurals, for input and output?
why.a_en: Arabic usually speaks of input and output as many items: الْمُدْخَلَات are the things put in, and الْمُخْرَجَات the things that come out. They're plurals of the participles of أَدْخَلَ, to put in, and أَخْرَجَ, to bring out.

selftest.q_en: What does a count of failed logins prove on its own?
selftest.why_en: A count is a fact; an attack is a conclusion.
